checkpoints: BullMQ treats every uncaught throw inside a job processor as a failed attempt and increments job.attemptsMade, unless the job was already rescheduled with job.moveToDelayed(...) before that throw — a plain throw new Error('circuit open') is indistinguishable from the receiver genuinely rejecting the call.

During a sustained downstream outage the circuit stays open (or keeps re-tripping from a failed half-open probe) across many consecutive delivery cycles for the same event, so each skipped cycle still burns one attempt — it takes several circuit-open cool-downs, not a single throw, to exhaust attemptsMade and park the event in dead_letter with attempts: 3 even though the receiver never actually saw the request.

The correct fix is a strict ordering rather than a different mechanism: await job.moveToDelayed(Date.now() + delay, token) must happen FIRST so BullMQ knows the job is already rescheduled, and only THEN should new DelayedError() be thrown — DelayedError is BullMQ's explicit 'already handled, don't count this' signal.

Thrown before moveToDelayed, or thrown as a plain Error at all, BullMQ has no way to distinguish the circuit-open skip from an ordinary failure and still counts it toward attemptsMade — the ordering, not the error type alone, is what makes the skip invisible to the retry accounting.

A circuit-open skip is an infrastructure decision made without ever contacting the receiver, while a failed attempt should only be recorded when the receiver was actually reached and rejected the request; conflating the two quietly corrupts the dead-letter table's meaning as a record of genuinely-exhausted deliveries.

The circuit's half-open state admits exactly one probe per cool-down, so if that probe request reuses the same soft-skip code path before its success or failure is recorded, it risks being miscounted as a burned attempt too — the fix needs to close that gap, not just the plain circuit-open branch.

With the ordering corrected, attemptsMade stays flat for as long as the circuit remains open no matter how many cool-down cycles the outage spans, and only events the receiver actually rejected MAX_ATTEMPTS times ever reach the dead-letter table.

A deterministic check for this fix drives a downstream outage across several consecutive circuit-open cool-downs and asserts the attempt counter stays unchanged throughout, then confirms that only events for which the receiver genuinely returned failures accumulate attempts and eventually land in dead_letter.
